steps.description: @assertion the startup "Welcome to VS Code" sign-in overlay is visible and its Close button is available.
Click the Close button on the startup Welcome sign-in overlay.
@assertion the startup sign-in overlay is no longer visible and the VS Code workbench is ready.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
@assertion the Visual Studio Code Command Palette is visible with a > character in its input box and is ready to accept a command search.

parameters.text: Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit: Focus on Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit View

steps.description: Type the resolved command title into the active Command Palette.

Type the resolved option label OAuth (with dynamic registration) into the active single-select prompt.

@assertion the active prompt titled Workspace Folder is visible and the option Default folder is focused.

@assertion the active prompt titled Application Name is visible.

Press Enter to submit the accepted text input.
@assertion the Preview README.md editor tab is open in Visual Studio Code.
Open a fresh terminal for the DCR update prepare stage.

Click the "Sign in" button within the Microsoft 365 developer sandbox modal.
@assertion the Microsoft Sign in page is visible in Chrome with an email or username input and a Next button.

Enter the resolved Microsoft 365 account name into the email or username input field on the Microsoft Sign in page.
@assertion the Microsoft Sign in page in Chrome shows ${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_NAME}} in the account input and a Next button.

Press Enter to submit the Microsoft 365 login form from the password entry screen.

parameters.text: Call the remote whoami tool. Show only tenant_id, auth_method, and client_id copied from its actual result as a short, pretty-printed JSON object. Do not infer or invent values.

steps.description: Type "Call the remote whoami tool. Show only tenant_id, auth_method, and client_id copied from its actual result as a short, pretty-printed JSON object. Do not infer or invent values." into the Copilot message input.
Press Enter to send the Copilot message.

@assertion the current Copilot turn requires authentication and shows an enabled Sign in to ${{var:app_name}} button alongside Cancel. This is the OAuth connection card, not an Allow capability-consent card.
Click the Sign in to ${{var:app_name}} button in the current Microsoft 365 Copilot turn to start the registered OAuth connection.

@assertion the active authorization popup is on the facade hosting ${{env:MCP_AUTH_ENDPOINT}} and shows Authorize an MCP client, a Client ID, Callback destination https://teams.microsoft.com/api/platform/v1.0/oAuthRedirect, and an enabled Allow this client button. No invalid_client or authorization error is visible.

Click Allow this client on the facade's Authorize an MCP client page to approve this dynamically registered client's displayed permissions and callback, then continue to Microsoft Entra authorization.

@assertion the active Microsoft sign-in popup shows Pick an account. The Signed in row for ${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_NAME}} has keyboard focus, indicated by its dotted outline. Use another account is not focused.
Press Enter to select the focused signed-in Microsoft account ${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_NAME}} and complete this OAuth authorization, not another account.

@assertion Microsoft 365 Copilot is active again with the owned agent ${{var:app_name}} and its message composer visible. No external authentication popup, Microsoft account-picker page, or pending Sign in to ${{var:app_name}} card is visible. Popup closure alone does not establish a completed tool invocation.
Press Escape in the active Copilot chat to dismiss the sidebar hover tooltip without dismissing the inline connection-consent card.
@assertion the Copilot action-consent Allow button is visible.
Click the "Allow" button in the Microsoft 365 Copilot chat interface to grant the agent access.
@assertion the Copilot action-consent Allow button is no longer visible.
@assertion the current assistant turn is complete and contains a non-empty response.

@assertion the current completed assistant response contains a returned result for the requested remote tool whoami. Returned tool-specific result data, including inline JSON, is sufficient evidence. Do not require a separate tool execution marker, citation, trace panel, debugger information, or developer mode. A user prompt, tool description, refusal, loading state, or promise to call without a result does not satisfy this assertion.

@assertion the current completed assistant tool result contains the field client_id with a non-empty string value. Missing, null, empty and whitespace-only values fail. Any non-empty identifier is acceptable; no specific literal value or JSON whitespace formatting is required. The field name in the user prompt or a tool description alone is not a result.
@assertion the current assistant response contains ""tenant_id": "${{env:MCP_AUTH_EXPECTED_TENANT}}"".
@assertion the current assistant response contains ""auth_method": "entra_user"".
@assertion the Microsoft 365 Copilot message input is visible in the open agent chat.
Click the "Message" input box in the Microsoft 365 Copilot web application.

@assertion the current assistant response contains ""auth_flow": "${{env:MCP_AUTH_EXPECTED_FLOW}}"".

@assertion the current assistant response contains ""server_time":".
